candidate.name: digit width
candidate.meaning: The number of bits in one digit; the letter changes meaning from the padded length on the earlier page.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of bits in the padded binary representation bin_k, that is, the length it pads to.

judged.note: Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: use another letter for the digit width (for example w or b) instead of k, since k is the padded length on the exact-integer-multiplication page. If k is kept, say on the page that it means digit width here.

candidate.name: first integer
candidate.meaning: The integer represented by the first input string.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A binary string of length n, the first factor of the product.

judged.note: Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: x there is the integer value, while on the exact-integer-multiplication page x is the binary string and val(x) is its integer. Use val(x) for the integer, or another letter for the integer, and keep x for the string where the string is meant.

candidate.name: second integer
candidate.meaning: The integer represented by the second input string.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A binary string of length n, the second factor of the product.

judged.note: Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: y there is the integer value, while on the exact-integer-multiplication page y is the binary string and val(y) is its integer. Use val(y) for the integer, or another letter, and keep y for the string where the string is meant.

candidate.name: coefficient position
candidate.meaning: The index of a coefficient of the product polynomial, running over $0,\dots,2d-2$; the letter changes meaning from the integer argument of $\mathrm{bin}_k$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The nonnegative integer, below 2^k, whose binary representation is taken.

judged.note: Radix-digit-convolution is the later page: use another letter (for example p or r) for the coefficient position, since m is the integer argument of bin_k on the exact-integer-multiplication page. If m is kept, say on the page that it is a coefficient position here.

candidate.name: cyclic axis count
candidate.meaning: The number of cyclic axes, which is the number of coordinates of a box point.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of digit positions in each padded input.

judged.note: Chinese-remainder-map is the later page: use another letter (for example r) for the number of cyclic axes, since d is the digit count on the radix-digit-convolution page. If d is kept, the page already says it is the axis count and not the digit count.

candidate.name: position
candidate.meaning: A position in the cyclic convolution, ranging over 0 to T-1.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of bits in each of the inputs x and y.

judged.note: Chinese-remainder-map is the later page: use another letter (for example p or u) for the cyclic position, since n is the input length on the exact-integer-multiplication page. The map page already flags this; avoid n for the position in any further use.

candidate.name: axis index
candidate.meaning: An index from $1$ to $d$ labelling the axes.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The imaginary unit, with i squared equal to -1.

judged.note: Prime-source-lengths is the later page: use another letter (for example j or a) for the axis index, since i is the imaginary unit on the gaussian-resampling page.

candidate.name: padded length variable
candidate.meaning: A real number standing for a large power-of-two padded length in the prime-count statement.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The integer represented by the first input string.

judged.note: Prime-source-lengths is the later page: use another letter (for example X or L) for the real padded-length variable, since x is the integer represented by the first input on the radix-digit-convolution page. If x is kept, say here that it is a real padded length, not the integer input.

candidate.name: padded length variable
candidate.meaning: A real number standing for a large power-of-two padded length in the prime-count statement.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A binary string of length n, the first factor of the product.

judged.note: Prime-source-lengths is the later page: use another letter (for example X or L) for the real padded-length variable, since x is the binary input string on the exact-integer-multiplication page. If x is kept, say here that it is a real padded length, not an input string.

candidate.name: cyclic position
candidate.meaning: A position on the cycle of length T, with 0 at most p less than T.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of a coefficient of the product, running over $0,\dots,2d-2$.

judged.note: The Chinese-remainder-map page is the later page, since it applies its map to the coefficients of radix-digit convolution. It should not reuse p for a cyclic position, because p there is the coefficient index running over 0,...,2d-2. Use another letter (for example k) for the cyclic position, or say explicitly that p means a cyclic position here and not the coefficient index of the radix-digit page.

candidate.name: output position
candidate.meaning: The position of an output coefficient of the convolution, with 0 at most w less than T.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of bits in one digit.

judged.note: The Chinese-remainder-map page is the later page. There w is an output position with 0 <= w < T, while on the radix-digit page w is the digit width in bits (B = 2^w). The map page should use another letter for the output position (for example v), or say that w here is an output position and not the digit width.

candidate.name: prime variable
candidate.meaning: A variable standing for a prime number.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A second position on the cycle of length T, with 0 at most q less than T.

judged.note: The prime-source-lengths page is the later page, since it builds on the Chinese-remainder map (its s_a are the moduli of that map). There it says 'Let q denote a prime', but q on the Chinese-remainder-map page is a second cyclic position with 0 <= q < T. The prime-source-lengths page should write the prime with another letter (for example r is taken, so use something like pi or ell), or say that q here is a prime and not the cyclic position of the map page.
